attrs.content: Not all contractors are created equal when it comes to home accessibility modifications. While general contractors, handymen, and specialized accessibility experts may all offer home improvement services, the level of expertise, training, and understanding of accessibility needs varies significantly.

General contractors are licensed professionals who can manage various home improvement projects. They may have experience with basic accessibility modifications but often lack specialized training in accessibility standards, adaptive equipment, and the unique needs of individuals with mobility challenges.

Handymen can handle small repairs and basic installations but typically lack the licensing, insurance, and specialized knowledge required for complex accessibility modifications. They may not be familiar with ADA guidelines, proper grab bar installation techniques, or the specific requirements of assistive equipment.

Specialized accessibility contractors like One Source Mobility combine general contracting licenses with advanced certifications in accessibility and home modification. They understand not just how to install equipment, but why specific modifications are needed and how to ensure they meet both regulatory standards and individual needs.

attrs.values:
• ATP (Assistive Technology Professional): Specialized expertise in assistive technology assessment and implementation
  • CAPS (Certified Aging-in-Place Specialist): Advanced training in designing spaces for aging in place
  • ECHM (Executive Certificate in Home Modification): Comprehensive knowledge of home modifications and accessibility
  • CLIPP (Certified Living In Place Professional): Expert in modifications for independent living
  • C.E.A.C. (Certified Environmental Access Consultant): Specialized in environmental accessibility and ADA compliance
